problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-4{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Distinct Eigenvalues

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Linear System of Differential Equations
examples.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=6{x}_{1}(t)+7{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_1=-1$ and $\lambda_2=3.$*
examples.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)$ for the given system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/39f5b156a53392174c4b0c490f01c7bb3fee6530fc5f1e2e16be43d0de99067b.png)

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are 

$$
\lambda_1=-1
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\lambda_2=3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1 =-1,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/62cc97bb07ba88adc4b9fc6b42f33c924bf8d1d38c38ecf29973264c6ac24ee2.png)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/96afd68567ff82d1a461ad2b38f9492f644982f7dc4628526945bd619335c5ff.png)

- For $\lambda_2 =3,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/27f4874dc20e09331a89c5135dcacff5d6cce93d6040fdac954845478324b58b.png)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067055/assets/6d3732ee67364278140c7e9ba5ec791cef69f4a60c8533d1f528c4bb5e718a35.png)

Thus, the general solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ respectively.
What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$
